content: The page continues a definition of the empty figure as the least element of the family of figures, then states that disjoint figures are compatible.

Equation (1.13) claims an equivalence between disjoint figures and shadow-disjointness explained by empty intersection plus compatibility of all shadow elements. The next paragraph reformulates this using lieux and atelier-disjointness.

The final paragraph says compatibility and disjunction matter on the subsets M and L. For set-theoretic ateliers the relations on L are called trivial: lieux are always compatible and disjoint exactly when distinct. The last sentence begins a qualification about the set-theoretic and moderate case and continues off-page.
math_reading_decisions: The right operand in the live equality and final column line is literally om(G); the b is not supplied from surrounding omb occurrences.
The column says compatible, while the prose says disjoint with the parenthetical atelier qualification. Both are retained; no mathematical harmonization is performed.
The first implication’s G is settled from its basal return, without relying solely on the F/G pairing.
The first family F retains genuine alphabet uncertainty; ordinary F variables remain distinct.
The bottom barred m is treated as a verbal abbreviation, probable expansion même, not an equality or quotation mark.
The potential canceled equality stroke is retained as uncertain; H’s empty set after that canceled equality is unsupported.
